gen-megrim-gf-aclonica: Sharp, futuristic, drawn with a single thread of ink. Megrim hands off to Aclonica, a sans with a deep midsection, a modest weight shift and widely spaced letters stretched along the line.
gen-megrim-gf-allerta: Allerta reads wide and loose, its tall x-height and generous tracking giving each line room. Megrim, with its constant-walled o, crowns the pair, and the text beneath drifts along at an easy pace.
gen-megrim-gf-alumni-sans-pinstripe: Approachable in manner, Alumni Sans Pinstripe packs its words tightly, with oversized lowercase letters set beside small capitals. Beneath angular Megrim headings, the text feels compact and quietly unhurried.
gen-megrim-gf-alumni-sans-sc: Megrim cuts every stroke to a single depth, angular and futuristic. Alumni Sans SC follows with squeezed spacing, oversized lowercase and stems a touch heavier than its hairlines, so text feels tight and tidy.
gen-megrim-gf-arsenal: Megrim draws each letter as a thread of ink. Arsenal, a sans-serif whose x-height nearly meets the capitals, knits its letters close so text feels snug and approachable.
gen-megrim-gf-basic: Basic reads straightforward and tidy, with only a gentle bump from small letters up to capitals. Megrim, traced with a plotter pen's single-weight line, adds the angular, futuristic edge while Basic keeps things low-key.
gen-megrim-gf-cal-sans: Angular, futuristic lettering with a measured, constant stroke up top. Megrim sets up the sharpness, then Cal Sans, with a single stroke width and tall x-height, brings approachable modern warmth.
gen-megrim-gf-inder: Clean and precise, Megrim draws angular, futuristic letters like thread stitched along a path. Inder, a sans with little height difference between its cases, settles into text at a gentle, steady pace.
gen-megrim-gf-major-mono-display: Angular and futuristic, with neon-glass glow in every curve. Megrim excels at the sharp, measured line, while Major Mono Display, a monospace with tube-like strokes and wide sidebearings, supplies precise, technical lettering.
gen-megrim-gf-matemasie: Megrim keeps its letters open and angular, each stroke ending at a single measured width. Matemasie, a sans-serif with broad gaps and small entry points into its round, closed letters, offers a grounded counterpart.
